messages:
Maya: FYI we're getting a cluster of customer reports with 429s and a few 401s right after the burst-rate policy canary went live at ~11:20 UTC.

Lina: Which canary cohort? We rolled burst_v2 to 10% at 11:20 — changes were smaller window + lower per-key burst cap.

Shawn: Can you paste a couple of sample logs / request IDs? I'll start tracing ingress paths.

Maya: sample logs pasted from customer A:
```
[2025-09-12T11:31:46Z] req_id=abc123 svc=ingress 429 reason=rate_limit policy=burst_v2 client=acme-inc
[2025-09-12T11:31:47Z] req_id=abc124 svc=ingress 401 reason=auth_failure token_expired=false client=acme-inc
[2025-09-12T11:31:48Z] req_id=abc125 svc=ingress 429 reason=rate_limit policy=burst_v2 client=acme-inc
```

Raj: We saw a correlated spike in auth errors from a subset of AZs around the same time — looks like token validation calls spiked and upstream auth returned transient 5xx -> surfaced as 401s.

Shawn: Hypothesis: the tighter burst window caused more simultaneous token validation/refresh requests. Auth service hit a transient overload and some checks failed. Need concrete repro.

Maya: Customer repro steps: "6 concurrent streaming generate calls using a single API key, small prompts, sustained for ~30s. After ~20s, about half the calls see 429 and one shows 401." They ran from a single region.

Lina: Can we limit this to canary customers only? If yes we should pause/roll back the canary while we debug.

Raj: I'm +1 for rollback. Recommend revert burst window to previous value and drop canary to 0% pending instrumentation.

deploy-bot: @Raj initiated canary rollback for config burst_v2 -> burst_v1. Rollback queued, expected completion ~2m.

Shawn: I'll add extra logging on the auth path and emit a temporary metric ingress.auth.transient_failures. Also instrument token refresh concurrency counters.

Maya: I'll update the affected customers and open tickets for anyone who pinged us. Marking this as P2 for now.

Elena: Notifying the high-touch customers now. ETA confirmation message to them in 30m.

Lina: Postmortem action items: revert now, then when green do a phased rollout: 1% -> 5% -> 10% with synthetic load that simulates token refresh churn. Example proposed canary config:
```
canary:
  pct: 1
  validation:
    error_rate_threshold: 0.5%  # overall
    auth_error_threshold: 0.1%   # auth-specific
burst_policy_v2:
  window_seconds: 60
  max_tokens: 10000
```

Raj: Rollback completed at 11:46 UTC. Monitoring for 30m.

Maya: Customer-side errors dropped after rollback in our samples. Closing thread for now — will reopen if we see reoccurrence. :thumbsup:
